as_told.title: Corso's co-author inserted fake material into the book

plain: Every story on this page was told on one podcast, American Alchemy, hosted by Jesse Michels. Michels says that Philip J. Corso, author of The Day After Roswell, a book published in 1997 about the crash people say happened near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947, got only 24 hours from his co-author, William J. Birnes, to edit it before it came out. Michels brings this up on three episodes. He calls it the reason there is "clearly some BS in that book". Once he also mentions an earlier draft by Corso called Dawn of a New Age, and once he passes on a claim from a researcher who goes by UAP Gerb: that the co-author "inserted all sorts of fake stuff in there almost to stigmatize Corso," which, if true, would mean the book's weakest parts were not Corso's own.
